thread:
Amy K: Quick snapshot from this morning's mini-sweep comparing L4 / T4 / A10G for embeddings and small-chat. TL;DR: cost per request and kernel choices drive a very different sweet spot depending on quant and context length.

Jordan P: nice, do you have p95 numbers? also region breakdown?

Amy K: p95 numbers below (avg over 1000 samples, 512 tok inputs for small-chat, 256 for embeddings). Regions: us-west1 / eu-west1 / asia-east1. Short list: 
- L4: p95 18ms (emb), 42ms (chat) us-west1, best throughput per GPU for fp16.
- T4: p95 27ms (emb), 65ms (chat) eu-west1, lower perf but cheapest spot pricing.
- A10G: p95 12ms (emb), 30ms (chat) us-west1, best latency but higher $/hour.

Satish R: what about int8 quant? quality hit?

Amy K: int8 (dynamic) results: embeddings cosine drop ~0.6% vs fp16 baseline for our eval set (semantic-qa). small-chat: automated BLEU/Rouge-style metric shows ~1.4% dip, but human spot-check found more hallucination in rare entity prompts. Overall we see quality regression concentrated in long-tail prompts.

Lina M: did you try kernel toggles (fused-attn, nvfuser-like path)?

Amy K: yes. On L4 and A10G the fused-attn kernel netted ~8-10% p95 win for chat; on T4 the fused kernel was unstable for 2k-context runs (OOMs) so we fell back to generic kernel. Code snippet we used to toggle:
```
# runtime config snippet
model.runtime.kernels = ["fused_attention", "matmul_fallback"]
model.runtime.quant = "int8_dynamic"
```
Jordan P: interesting. So T4's kernel support is the blocker for small-chat at higher contexts. Any region-specific surprises?

Amy K: asia-east1 had slightly worse T4 p95s (~+15%) — we suspect NV driver versions differ and the optimized kernel isn't available/compiled there. A10G was consistent across regions. L4 had better throughput in eu-west1 due to higher rack density (we could pack 6 models per host without hitting mem).

Satish R: cost numbers per 1M requests? ballpark please.

Amy K: rough econ (hosted pricing proxies + infra amort):
- L4 (fp16): $28 / 1M small-chat requests; embeddings: $7 / 1M
- T4 (fp16): $14 / 1M small-chat; embeddings: $3.5 / 1M
- A10G (fp16): $42 / 1M small-chat; embeddings: $10 / 1M
Switching to int8 drops the per-request compute cost ~20% on L4/A10G but only ~8% on T4 (kernel inefficiencies).

Lina M: capacity sizing for 200 rps chat (512 tok) — how many GPUs each?

Amy K: ballpark sustained throughput per GPU at target latencies:
- L4: ~250 rps (so 1 GPU handles 200 rps comfortably, ops headroom for spikes)
- T4: ~100 rps (so 2+ GPUs recommended with autoscale)
- A10G: ~380 rps (1 GPU overkill, can consolidate many customers)
So T4 forces more headcount in reserved capacity, which changes cost calculus.

Jordan P: any notable failure modes during quant bring-up?

Amy K: yes — two things: (1) int8 dynamic on T4 underflows on narrow distribution tokens, causing repeated async casts and slower kernel launches; (2) A small subset of prompts on L4-int8 produced a tokenization edge-case that caused score drift — fixed by clamping softmax for underflow tokens. We added a regression test that covers the top 50 proximate prompts.

bench-bot: auto-attach: /artifacts/1765550000-mini-sweep-raw.csv (s3://redwood-bench/eng-ml/1765550000.csv)

Satish R: can you add the eval set that showed the 0.6% embedding drop? want to run our reranker through it.

Amy K: uploaded as /datasets/sem-qa-2026-v1.csv and linked it in the artifact. Also pushed a small script to repro quant vs fp16 comparisons:
```bash
python bench_run.py --model rwd-smallchat-v1 --quant int8 --region us-west1 --kernels fused_attention --samples 1000
```

Lina M: proposal: for hosted default we should expose fp16 L4 and A10G for latency-sensitive routes, T4-int8 as low-cost fallback for embeddings-heavy routes, and have a routing policy that pins by SLO and cost threshold. I can draft a rollout plan.

Jordan P: agree. Also flagging we should add driver/kernel version checks in the deployer so T4 fallbacks are automatic across regions.

Amy K: noted. I'll add a follow-up doc with numbers + recommended routing thresholds. Quick action items:
- Amy: publish sweep summary + artifacts (today)
- Lina: draft routing + rollout (EOD tomorrow)
- Satish: run reranker eval on sem-qa set (tomorrow)
- Jordan: add deployer kernel checks (this week)

Satish R: thanks, that helps a lot.

Amy K: thanks all :thumbsup:
